title: tool-calling: improve execution ergonomics for parallel multi-tool calls, result injection, and retries
author: Aisha Patel
ci_checks: bench: added micro-bench for parallel tool dispatch: pass
body: Summary: This PR improves the tool-calling execution ergonomics in several ways: 1) enables parallel dispatch of independent tool calls requested in a single model response, 2) standardizes and hardens tool result injection into the response generation loop (ensuring deterministic insertion points for streaming), and 3) adds a lightweight retry/backoff mechanism for transient tool failures with idempotency hints. Motivation: customer workloads increasingly rely on multi-tool orchestration (search + DB + external API) issued from a single model turn. Previously our executor handled tool calls sequentially by default which increased tail latency for independent tools and made streaming/result-injection ordering fragile for partial outputs. Design: - API surface: no breaking API changes for OpenAI-compat or Redwood API. Introduce an opt-in field on the tool-calling execution plan: "parallel_tools": "auto|on|off" (default auto). Auto enables parallel dispatch when the analysis phase proves tool independence (no shared mutable temp bindings) or when user explicitly requests parallelism. - Execution: tool executor will group independent tools and dispatch them concurrently using the runtime's async workers. Results are associated with tool call IDs and injected back into the generation context at well-defined markers (tool_result(<id>)) to preserve deterministic streaming. - Injection: result injection is now performed via a two-phase commit: discovery of injection markers in the in-progress tokenstream and an ordered apply step that supports incremental streaming to the client. This avoids races where partial tool results could interleave incorrectly with generated text. - Retries: added configurable retry policy per tool call (attempts, initial_backoff_ms, max_backoff_ms) and an optional idempotency token to guard against side-effecting tools. Retry telemetry is exposed via metrics when retries are used. - OpenAI-compat layer: preserved compatibility with existing function call semantics. When parallel_tools is on, function-calling payloads are still encoded to match OpenAI schema; we added explicit hints in the compat layer so downstream SDKs can surface the new behavior. Backwards compatibility: default behavior remains effectively unchanged (auto throttles parallelism conservatively). Existing clients that don't pass parallel_tools continue to see previous semantics. Implementation notes: - New runtime module: redwood/runtime/tool_executor_v2.py implements grouping, async dispatch, and injection logic. - Compat layer updates: redwood/api/openai_compat.py maps OpenAI function call requests to the new execution plan and preserves legacy flags. - Docs: redwood-docs/api/tool-calling.md documents the parallel_tools option and recommends idempotency patterns. - Tests: extensive unit and integration tests added. Benchmarks show ~25-40% tail latency improvement for multi-tool (3+ independent tools) scenarios. Rollout plan: feature gated behind a runtime flag (tool_calling_v2_enabled) and rolled out first to dedicated instances for soak testing, then wider in hosted. Metrics and alerting added to detect increased error/retry rates. Checklist: - [x] design doc updated and linked - [x] unit tests - [x] integration tests - [x] docs - [x] bench added - [x] compatibility tests - [x] metrics/alerting added

aisha/compat: wire openai_compat to execution plan and add hints for parallelism
aisha/tests: add unit/integration tests for parallel dispatch, injection, and retries
aisha/docs: document parallel_tools option and idempotency guidance
aisha/bench: micro-benchmark for multi-tool tail latency
review_comments: Jonah Keefe (2026-02-19): Good direction. A few questions: how do we guarantee ordering for streaming when a later tool result arrives before an earlier one? Can we avoid buffering the whole stream?

Aisha Patel (reply 2026-02-19): We use ordered injection by marker ID and stream partial placeholders ("[tool <id> pending]") to clients until result arrives; once ready we replace the placeholder with the result delta. This adds small buffering per-marker but not whole-response buffering.
Lina Martinez (2026-02-20): Please add more tests for idempotency token handling and side-effecting tools. Also nit: separate the backoff params into a small config object.
Aisha Patel (reply 2026-02-21): Added tests for idempotency and refactored retry params into RetryPolicy in tool_calling_schema.py.
Ethan Brooks (2026-02-22): CI integration tests flaky on CI image; saw a transient DNS failure causing retries to spike. Suggest a test harness stub to make tests deterministic.
Aisha Patel (reply 2026-02-23): Added a network stub for the integration test and marked the flaky case with feature flag so CI runs deterministic path by default.
Jonah Keefe (approval 2026-02-25): Approving, small doc nits addressed in follow-up.
release_notes: Improve tool-calling ergonomics: parallel dispatch of independent tools, deterministic result injection for streaming, and configurable retries with idempotency tokens.
No breaking changes; behavior default remains conservative (auto).
Recommended: use idempotency tokens for side-effecting tools when enabling parallelism.
